The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for many shoppers
Why, in plain words: Switching on a new feature made the account page use a new monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month because it ends up dividing by zero.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 38.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,182.30 USD {customer_loss}
- People who responded: 2 {responders}
- Their time, added together: 17 min {engineer_minutes}

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #552 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for many shoppers while monthly-spend-feature was on
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 03:46 to 03:54 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:12:41 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:52:35 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 03:46 UTC and was back to normal at 03:54 UTC, 8 minutes later. 26.5% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 38.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 5,182.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching on a new feature made the account page use a new monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month because it ends up dividing by zero. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #552, for a person to review and merge. Code-Fix's reading says the faulty calculation was still in the code: switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month, and with the flag off, the older calculation can still fail for accounts with no purchases at all.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
38.5% - peak error rate
2,544 - requests failed
1.0% to 26.5% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
5,182.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The function the flag turned on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, divides the account's total spent this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month` and has no answer for an empty list. For any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError at the line the logs name, so every account page request for such a shopper failed once monthly-spend-feature sent the page's spend figure through it. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers opening their account page got a failed request instead of the page, and the service's share of failed requests rose sharply.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 occurrences in 9 minutes, 03:44–03:52; # was 0.50% to 38.50%, typically 28.00%, highest at 03:47
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:46–03:52
why 1 Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero, raised in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The error shows up in the logs from the onset until the logs that were read end.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    Gbac1
why 2 The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at 03:46:28 UTC. The flag's evaluations went from all off, to a mix of on and off at the onset, to all on right after it.
  Evidence:
    P1 03:46:28 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 03:44–03:45
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 / on 102 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:46
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 03:47–03:52
  Ruled out:
    A deployment: the production change events read back for the day before the onset held only this flag change, and no deploy came back.
      T8 03:53:01 Investigator Agent: Read back 1 production change
      P1
    Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read, and that was this one.
      T14 03:53:03 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 03:53:03
      P1
    The client-disconnect failures on the account page: these were seen before the onset, while the account page error rate was still low. The division-by-zero failures appear only once the flag went on.
      G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 3 occurrences in 2 minutes, 03:44–03:45
      Gbac1
      G5309
why 3 With the flag on, the account page's spend figure goes through a new monthly per-item average that divides by the number of this month's purchases, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- The flag switch reached all of the account page's traffic at once: its evaluations went from all off to all on almost immediately. No staged rollout and no error-rate check that would halt it were seen. (AI-3, AI-4)
- Before the flag was switched on in production, no test was seen that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases in the current month. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 03:46:28 UTC. That enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 30%. No deployment was involved. | 0.95 | confirmed

Trigger
monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 03:46:28 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 03:53:15 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 03:56:44 | Proposed a fix: PR #552 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 03:46 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 03:52:14 UTC, 6 minutes 14 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #552 | open
AI-3 | Roll out feature flag changes on io-shop in stages, starting with a small share of traffic, instead of switching them on for all traffic at once. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Halt and revert a staged flag rollout automatically when the service's error rate rises while it is under way. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Require tests that run each flag-gated code path with its flag on, including for shoppers with no purchases in the current month, to pass before that flag can be switched on in production. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Decide whether `average_spend_per_item`, used while the flag is off, should keep raising for an account with no purchases at all. Code-Fix reports that the current tests expect it to raise. | prevent | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 49 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute 1 second after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 2 minutes 57 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes 30 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #552.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 11 03:46 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began

T6 | 03:53 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
T7 | 03:53:01 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 03:47
T8 | 03:53:01 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 1 production change

Response effort
17 min - engineer time, 2 responders
144,103 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/620f6b64-dd80-4758-941c-0f7387fe3dcb
The fix it proposed: PR #552 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/552) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 03:46:28 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 03:44–03:45
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 3 occurrences in 2 minutes, 03:44–03:45
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 occurrences in 9 minutes, 03:44–03:52; # was 0.50% to 38.50%, typically 28.00%, highest at 03:47
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 / on 102 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:46
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:46–03:52
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 03:47–03:52
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides account.total_this_month_cents by len(bought_this_month), the number of purchases flagged in_current_month. Most shoppers have bought before but not this month. For them that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. That is the line the incident log names (spend_summary.py:47). Turning on monthly-spend-feature sent the account page's figure through this function, and every request for such a shopper failed.

The flag was what triggered the incident, but the fault is in the code: the function has no answer for the normal case of a shopper who has bought nothing this month. With the fix, when there are no purchases this month the function returns 0, because a shopper with no purchases this month has spent nothing this month. Otherwise it divides as before. Shoppers who did buy this month get the same result as before.

Other code is unchanged. With the flag off, render_spend_summary still uses average_spend_per_item, and that function still raises for an account with no purchases at all. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py expect that error, and that error is the only case the line-number test in test_account_page.py checks. Nothing in this change catches errors.

The tests: the new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py call average_spend_per_item_this_month and render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) for a shopper whose purchases all fall outside the current month, and assert 0. Against the current code both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, account pages failed for some shoppers for {duration}, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. The failures began when a new feature was switched on that made the account page use a new monthly spending calculation. That calculation likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, because it ends up dividing by zero. Argus estimates the lost takings at {customer_loss}. {responders} people responded, spending {engineer_minutes} of their time in total. Argus turned the feature back off by reverting the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, and that reversal is confirmed and still in place. Argus has also proposed a permanent fix, but it is only a draft pull request and has not been put into use.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
